name: R4KVV devnet r4 keeper test
seriesTitle: U.S. national debt (Debt to the Penny)

rules.statement: Each time the treasury.debt feed settles, every full 1000000000 above the previous settlement is one unit, and the keeper spends 1% of the fee pool buying the token at market and burns everything received per unit (buyback spend compounds: pool × (1 − (1 − f)^units)). A voided market burns nothing. Settled results only; prices are never read. When the rule ends with a result, whatever is left in the burn pool moves to $DEFICIT's burn pool (the platform's flagship coin) and burns that coin, and so does any fee income that arrives after that; nothing is refunded and nobody is paid. When the rule ends void (a voided market, a voided pair or a cancelled season), whatever is left burns down on this coin on a daily clock over four weeks (at least 99% of it), then the coin retires, and later fee income is swept and burned whenever it passes 0.05 SOL (at most once a week).

pool.queuedNote: Before the audit, burns spend from at most 25 SOL. Fee income above that is held and released after the audit. The keeper enforces this cap today, and the program enforces it once it is deployed.

fees.sentence: On every 1 SOL traded on the curve, 0.0025 SOL to Raydium, 0.0025 SOL to Burnticker (developer) and 0.005 SOL to the burn pool (1% in all). After graduation, each trade in the Raydium pool pays 0.5% in fees. 100% of the liquidity is locked forever, and its fees fund the burn. Of the 0.0021 SOL per 1 SOL that the liquidity earns, 0.00168 SOL goes to the burn pool and 0.00042 SOL goes to the operator. That 80/20 split is fixed in code, and the coin side of those fees is burned. The burn pool also gets Raydium's fixed CPMM creator fee of 0.0025 SOL per 1 SOL. The coin's creator on LaunchLab is the burn program's fee account, so the creator-fee slot can only pay the burn pool. The human creator receives no cash from fees, and the keeper only pays network fees.

disclosure.disclaimer: A memecoin. The rule says what the supply does, not what the price does. The rule is locked at launch and cannot be changed by anyone, including the creator. Burns are funded by the token's own trading fees (or a disclosed vault), recomputable by anyone from the public source and the published rule. Nobody is promised anything.

can: submit a settled reading it read from the public source
crank a burn the rule computes from that reading
raise or lower the developer fee within 0..500 bps for new trades
change the LP split for future graduations
deploy new program code once 2 of 3 approve a Squads proposal. The current time lock could not be read from chain just now; the current status above says more.
cannot: burn more than the rule says
withdraw from any fee PDA or vault
change any token's rule or burn
change the creator fee above 50 bps (program cap)

redirect a coin's Fee Key or LP fees (initialize_token and every buyback crank refuse a platform whose lock-NFT wallet is not the burn program's fee-keys PDA or whose LP is not 100 % locked; the 80/20 claim split is compiled)
anything without a new deployment, which is public
change a token's rule, readings or receipts after the fact, because the registry is append-only and database triggers enforce that
earn from a burn pool, because nothing is ever taken from one
